clue.text: Composer starts losing tempo, say, gutted

indicators.note: losing means the letter for tempo is dropped from the word for starts

parts.note: starts as nouns are debuts, first appearances
T is the standard abbreviation for tempo

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A composer's opening bars lose their pace, as if the music had been disembowelled.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBUTS minus T gives DEBUS; 'say, gutted' leaves just the S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French impressionist composer whose works fill this puzzle.

clue.text: Trace source of echo in Verdi orchestration

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
orchestration means arranging music, so the letters of the name are arranged anew

parts.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Tracing where an echo comes from in a Verdi score.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to trace its origin or source.

clue.text: British and German article abroad makes a pile

parts.note: und is the German for and
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A British and German item sent overseas becomes a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle is a heap of things tied or gathered together.

clue.text: Initially, stiff drink damages penile extensions?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word stiff

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
scars as a verb means damages or marks

explanation.surface: A risque line about a stiff drink harming certain male appendages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: flashy sports cars are often said to compensate for male inadequacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy sports cars are mocked as extensions of their owners' manhood.

clue.text: This is not art, perhaps — and trained Tyroleans do it

definitions.text: This is not art, perhaps — and trained Tyroleans do it

indicators.note: trained means drilled into new order, so the letters are reorganised

parts.note: the full pool of letters from which the answer and the other phrase are made
the letters to set aside from the pool, leaving the answer

explanation.surface: A dig that this mountain singing is not art, though trained Tyroleans perform it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer: the answer plus IS NOT ART rearranged gives TYROLEANS DO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is the warbling Alpine singing style practised in the Tyrol.

clue.text: Performers are childless reformers

indicators.note: childless says the abbreviation for child, CH, is removed

parts.note: Chartists were 19th-century British campaigners for electoral reform

explanation.surface: A remark that performers are reformers without children.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s-40s demanding votes for all men; CH is a dictionary abbreviation for child.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists are people who perform, as on a bill of entertainers.

clue.text: Check old song picked up in music halls

parts.note: an audit is a check of accounts

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Checking an old song that has been taken up in music halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria are halls where audiences listen to performances.

clue.text: Rang, say, and drove home

indicators.note: say signals that a word is spoken, giving a match in sound

parts.note: tolled means rang, as a bell

explanation.surface: Someone rang and then drove home.
explanation.definitionFit: Told in the sense of made an impression, as a point that told or hit home.

clue.text: Rolls here supported with drink

parts.note: sided with means supported
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Bread rolls here, served with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like bread or cars; it is drum rolls, played on this drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Snare-drum rolls are played on a side drum.

clue.text: Step unsteadily over tiny adult plant

indicators.note: over means covering, so the shuffled letters go round another piece
unsteadily suggests a wobbling step, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: wee means tiny in Scottish English
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: Treading shakily over a small grown-up plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' turns STEP into STPE, which goes 'over' WEE to make SWEETPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden flower.

clue.text: Rare working party piece that's repeated

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An unusual working party performs a piece that keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form whose main theme returns again and again between episodes.

clue.text: Traditional Gaelic music performed with delay now and then on river

parts.note: did means performed, as in did a dance

indicators.note: now and then picks every other letter of the word delay

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also one in Wales and England

explanation.surface: Folk music played with occasional hesitation by a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Diddly-dee is an informal name for jigging Irish or Scottish folk tunes.

clue.text: Mercurial character in book: it's set in turbulent Italy

parts.note: vol is short for volume, a book

indicators.note: set in says one piece is placed inside the shuffled letters
turbulent means stirred up, so the letters of Italy are mixed

parts.note: it, with the 's as a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A fickle character in a novel is placed in a turbulent Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' makes ATILY from Italy; the shuffled letters must also take in the small piece to give ATILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Volatility is a changeable, unpredictable temperament, which is what mercurial describes.

clue.text: Woman doesn't finish change

indicators.note: doesn't finish says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Edith is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman leaves something incomplete and alters it.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to alter or revise a text.

clue.text: Dragonfly from French-German river I caught

parts.note: de is the French for from

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so the river holds the letter

parts.note: the Moselle flows through France, Luxembourg and Germany

explanation.surface: A dragonfly from a Franco-German river that I caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoiselle is a name for a slender damselfly, a dragonfly-like insect.

clue.text: 1 across piece, a version of Cinderella, captivates its composer's heart

indicators.note: captivates means holds captive, so one piece holds the other inside it
a version of the name signals its letters rearranged
heart takes the central letter of the composer's name

parts.note: the composer of the piece is 1 across, Debussy

explanation.surface: A Debussy work as a retelling of Cinderella, holding the composer's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of DEBUSSY, U, goes inside an anagram of CINDERELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Clair de Lune is the famous third movement of Debussy's Suite bergamasque.

clue.text: A very quiet Scottish singer nearly died, clapped out?

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, means very quiet in music

indicators.note: nearly says the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music-hall singer

explanation.surface: A soft-voiced Scottish singer almost dies: is he worn out?
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lauder was a hugely popular Scottish music-hall entertainer. 'Clapped out' usually means worn out; here it is read as cheered off.
explanation.definitionFit: Applauded means greeted with clapping, a pun on clapped out.

clue.text: I worried about short solo by daughter, being unaccompanied

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: ate in the sense of what's eating you, i.e. worried

indicators.note: short says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: I fretted over a brief solo by my daughter, playing alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the final O from solo; 'about' has the pronoun plus the word for worried wrapped round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means set apart and alone, which is to be unaccompanied.

clue.text: See 22
An opera is rewritten to include Queen's instrument

indicators.note: to include says the shuffled letters hold another piece
rewritten means the letters of the words are set out afresh

parts.note: QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An opera is revised so that a royal instrument is added to the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A square piano is an early rectangular, horizontal piano, a predecessor of the upright.

clue.text: Black Magic represented as fast food

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades

indicators.note: represented as signals the letters of the word presented in a new form

explanation.surface: Black Magic chocolates reworked as a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Magic is a British boxed chocolate brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Mac is McDonald's signature burger, a staple of fast food.

clue.text: Irish Republican breaks law over in part of Merseyside

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so one piece goes into the other
over in the sense of turned over, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irish Republican lawbreaker in a corner of north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LAW into WAL, and IRR 'breaks' it. The Wirral is a peninsula near Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wirral peninsula is partly within the county of Merseyside.

clue.text: Radical Paris edition of the Pink 'Un?

parts.note: le is the French for the, so a Paris version of the word
the Financial Times, FT, printed on pink paper, is nicknamed the Pink 'Un

explanation.surface: Musing whether a French edition of the Financial Times would be radical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British business daily printed on salmon-pink paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically, radical views are those on the left wing.

clue.text: Engineer made Freudian slip describing middle of tune, 1 across piece

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the shuffled letters enclose another piece
engineer as a verb means contrive or rearrange, signalling the letters are reorganised
middle of takes the central two letters of the word tune

explanation.surface: Someone engineered a Freudian slip in describing the middle of a Debussy tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; 'describing' means drawing a line round, so the shuffled letters enclose the centre of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune is Debussy's orchestral tone poem after Mallarmé.

clue.text: Seizes women leaving bars with no music?

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter for women is removed

parts.note: wrests means seizes forcibly

explanation.surface: Someone grabs women as they leave the pubs, silent ones with no music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs; in a score, a rest marks silence, so a bar of rests has no music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rests are silent intervals in a musical score.

clue.text: 2 of banknotes offering security

indicators.note: of indicates the answer is taken from part of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bundle of banknotes offers some financial security.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is BUNDLE; a knot is slang for a roll of banknotes, and a knot also secures things.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot can mean a cluster or roll, as of banknotes, much like a bundle.

clue.text: Steak went off stuffed with duck (extra large)

indicators.note: stuffed with means one piece is filled with the other

parts.note: turned means went off, as milk going sour
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
OS stands for outsize, extra large

explanation.surface: A steak that has gone off, filled with an oversized duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, hence O; OS (outsize) is a clothing size label.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos is a thick round cut of beef fillet.

clue.text: Not as convincing as 1 across piece

definitions.meaning: a weaker, less persuasive excuse, comparative of a feeble one
Debussy's orchestral sketches of the sea, first performed in 1905

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of lame, meaning feebler; the other names Debussy's symphonic sea portrait.

clue.text: Played together better stripped — Moore's outstanding

indicators.note: outstanding read as standing outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: Dud was the nickname of the comedian and pianist Dudley Moore

indicators.note: stripped removes the outer letters of the word better

explanation.surface: Two performers played together better unclothed, with Moore the star.
explanation.walkthrough: Dudley Moore was a British comic actor and jazz pianist, known as Dud in his sketches with Peter Cook.
explanation.definitionFit: To duet is to perform as a pair, so duetted means played together.

clue.text: Use it to trace letters from angry clients

indicators.note: angry suggests the clients are agitated, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to copy out the letters from cross customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template through which letters are painted or traced.
